newsitem.title: INDIA: Five trapped, one dead in India landslide.
newsitem.headline: Five trapped, one dead in India landslide.

text.p: Six people were feared crushed to death after a landslide struck their village on the outskirts of Bombay on Friday, police and witnesses said.
Mud and boulders buried five huts at Asalpha village in Ghatkopar, 25 km northeast of Bombay, after monsoon rains loosened the sides of a hill overlooking their homes, witnesses said.
The body of a 35-year-old man had been recovered and rescuers were searching for a family of five, but relatives feared they were dead.

"My daughter, son-in-law and their three children were having lunch when the hill came down," said a weeping Bismillah Sheikh Khwaja, 60. "They're trapped there, but I think they must be dead by now."
Fire brigade officials said it would take them five or six hours to clear away the debris.
"The rescue operation will take a lot of time," said deputy chief fire officer D.S. Mulye. "It's a lot of hard stone that has fallen on the hut and it will have to be cut away."
Four migrant labourers died in a similar incident in the northwestern suburb of Kandivli on Thursday.
